newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian refiners seen aiming for value added output.
newsitem.headline: Asian refiners seen aiming for value added output.

text.p: The price spread between light and heavy oil products will widen to a level that would eventually lead to an increase in the building of secondary processing plants, a consultant said on Wednesday.
Michael Krenek, a consultant with Ernst & Young/Wright Killen, told the 12th Asia-Pacific Petroleum Conference he expected light/heavy price spreads "to increase over the next several years,"
Light oil products are made up of gasoline, naphtha, diesel and jet fuel while fuel oil is the main heavy oil producs that emerges from refineries.

In the next few years, the supply of heavy oil product would be more than that of light products due to the additions of simple crude distillation units in the Asia-Pacific region and limited plans to add sophisticated processing units, Krenek said.
The continued substitution of natural gas for residual oil in heating and power generation would led to a drop in demand for the heavy product, he added.
Krenek said that after 2000, Asia Pacific refining processes would intensify and refiners operating simple CDUs would undertake investments to build sophisticated plants.
These new units would include hydrocrackers and fluid catalytic crackers -- plants that would refine the heavy oil product into the more lucrative light product.
